plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter, often while snow is still on the ground. It is widely cultivated in Japan, China, and Korea, and it is celebrated in poetry, painting, and festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: East Asia (Japan, China, Korea); cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom in the harshest part of winter, and the fruit is used to make umeboshi (pickled plums) and plum wine.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It carpets woodlands and gardens, often pushing up through frost and thin snow.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A fast-growing evergreen tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow pom-pom flower clusters. In Australia, wattles are an important food source for native insects and birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in Australia (July to October), with some Acacia species blooming in summer in the southern hemisphere
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Plumeria rubra
plants.description: A tropical deciduous tree with thick succulent branches and clusters of waxy, intensely fragrant flowers. In warm regions it can flower for many months, and it is often used in leis and temple offerings.
plants.bloomingSeason: Year-round in tropical climates, with strong flowering in warm, dry months
plants.location: Central America and Mexico; widely grown in Hawaii, the Caribbean, South Asia, and Southeast Asia
plants.funFact: The flowers are most fragrant at night to attract sphinx moths, yet the blooms offer no nectar and trick the moths into pollinating them.
